title: ipc: Finish ingress modularization and dedupe
description:
SECTION 0 CLARIFICATIONS
- Scope is vb_ipc module boundary cleanup; preserve public API compatibility.

SECTION 1 EARS REQUIREMENTS
- THE SYSTEM SHALL have one canonical MemoryIngress, IngressFrame, QueueCapacity, MaxPayloadBytes, and BoundedPayload implementation.
- WHEN existing callers import public vb_ipc symbols, THE SYSTEM SHALL preserve stable re-exports or provide compile-time migration inside the workspace.
- IF duplicate type definitions remain in lib.rs and split modules, THE SYSTEM SHALL NOT consider the refactor complete.

SECTION 2 CONTRACTS
- Preconditions: read crates/vb_ipc/src/lib.rs, ingress.rs, bounded.rs, tests.rs.
- Postconditions: lib.rs is a facade/re-export layer for ingress/bounded/error/frame modules where feasible.
- Invariants: bounded memory ingress remains bounded; Full/Disconnected/Empty behavior remains unchanged; payload size validation remains parse-don't-validate.

SECTION 2.5 RESEARCH
- Files: crates/vb_ipc/src/lib.rs lines around 654-798; crates/vb_ipc/src/ingress.rs; crates/vb_ipc/src/bounded.rs; crates/vb_ipc/src/tests.rs.

SECTION 3 INVERSION
- Failure: breaking public imports. Prevention: re-export old public names.
- Failure: two definitions diverge again. Prevention: delete duplicate implementation and add tests through public API.

SECTION 4 ATDD
- Happy: MemoryIngress::bounded accepts and receives frames through public API.
- Happy: payload limit allows valid payloads.
- Error: full queue maps to IpcError::Full.
- Error: oversized payload maps to IpcError::PayloadTooLarge.

SECTION 5 E2E
- IPC tests compile and pass; downstream crates using vb_ipc compile.

SECTION 5.5 VERIFICATION
- Scoped vb_ipc tests plus moon ci before landing.

SECTION 6 IMPLEMENTATION
- Make split modules authoritative.
- Turn lib.rs into facade and re-export stable symbols.
- Update imports/tests.

SECTION 7 FAILURE MODES
- Duplicate definitions remain; public API break; disconnected/full mapping changes.

SECTION 8 COMPLETION
- One canonical implementation only.
- lib.rs line count reduced substantially.

dependencies.title: architecture: Standardize queue and state boundaries
dependencies.description:
Planner/go-skill parent epic for architecture standardization.

SECTION 0 CLARIFICATIONS
- Resolved: FSM library selection is deferred. This epic must not add rust-fsm, smlang, statig, flume, kanal, thingbuf, or bbqueue.
- Resolved: Master document controls architecture choices.
- Resolved: Use battle-tested library primitives for mechanics, but keep domain wrappers local so queue/state meaning is not erased.

SECTION 1 EARS REQUIREMENTS
- THE SYSTEM SHALL standardize bounded queue use according to the master document: ArrayQueue for hot bounded MPMC runtime queues, rtrb for true SPSC rings, crossbeam_channel::bounded only for cold/blocking/UI boundaries.
- THE SYSTEM SHALL keep JournalWriterQueue as a storage-owned bounded batch/durability component, not a generic channel wrapper.
- WHEN state transitions are applied, THE SYSTEM SHALL route them through explicit transition APIs or canonical transition tables.
- IF an implementation attempts an unbounded runtime channel, THE SYSTEM SHALL NOT accept the change because it violates bounded-resource architecture.

SECTION 2 CONTRACTS
- Preconditions: master doc has been read; no production code changes happen outside Go-skill isolated workspace; bd tracks all child work.
- Postconditions: child beads define atomic implementation work; Go-skill can run each through explore/contract/proof/test/implementation/review/evidence/landing.
- Invariants: no unbounded queue introduction; no external FSM library addition in this epic; no merged state enum across bounded contexts.

SECTION 2.5 RESEARCH REQUIREMENTS
- Read velvet-ballistics-MASTER.md Library Choices and Section 45.
- Read queue/state surfaces before writing code.
- Verify public API compatibility for vb_ipc and runtime state changes.

SECTION 3 INVERSION
- Failure: generic queue abstraction erases domain semantics. Prevention: domain wrappers remain local.
- Failure: proof/runtime state drift persists. Prevention: parity tests and formal/proof artifact updates.
- Failure: planner work becomes mega-refactor. Prevention: atomic child beads.

SECTION 4 ATDD
- Child beads must include happy/error tests and contract tests for queue full, shutdown, parity, and illegal transitions.

SECTION 5 E2E
- Full epic complete only after all child beads pass moon ci, reviews, truth-serum evidence, landing, bd close/sync.

SECTION 5.5 VERIFICATION
- Go-skill full lifecycle required for each child bead.
- Dependency audit only if dependency files change.

SECTION 6 IMPLEMENTATION TASKS
- Execute children independently; do not combine unrelated queue and state changes.

SECTION 7 FAILURE MODES
- Direct runtime_states mutation remains; duplicate IPC definitions remain; UI unbounded channel remains; JournalWriterQueue semantics weaken.

SECTION 8 COMPLETION CHECKLIST
- All child beads closed and pushed.
- No new external FSM/channel dependency added.
- No unbounded channel remains in scoped IPC bridge path.
- StepState parity agrees with master Section 45.

SECTION 9 CONTEXT
- See child beads for exact files and acceptance gates.

SECTION 10 AI HINTS
- Do not use TodoWrite. Do not implement from source checkout. Use Go-skill isolation.
dependencies.notes: Demoted 2026-05-14: umbrella includes non-engine queue/state/UI work; core runtime children remain P0 where they directly support engine completion.

dependents.title: ipc/orchestrator: Prove local binary ingress synchronization
dependents.description: Prove local binary IPC ingress and runtime orchestration semantics for core engine use: compiled/artifact digest submit, bounded ingress, cancellation versus completion, timer ordering, shutdown drain, and slow-client/backpressure behavior.
dependents.acceptance_criteria: IPC SubmitRun or equivalent artifact-digest path reaches strict runtime admission; bounded queues reject with typed backpressure; cancel/completion/timer/shutdown races are deterministic and tested; no task-per-step or unbounded buffer behavior appears.
